question: Explain the principle of a moving coil galvanometer without using a diagram. Obtain the relation between current and deflection in a radial magnetic field. State why the scale of such a galvanometer is linear.

options.A: The galvanometer works because a current-carrying coil experiences a force parallel to the magnetic field. In a radial field, $\tau=NIAB\cos\theta=0$, so the scale is linear.
options.B: The galvanometer operates on electromagnetic induction. The relation is $I\propto1/\phi$, so its scale is linear.
options.C: A moving coil galvanometer works on the torque on a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field. In a radial field, $\theta=90^\circ$ always, so deflecting torque is $NIAB$. At equilibrium, $NIAB=k\phi$, hence $I=\dfrac{k}{NAB}\phi$. Thus $I\propto\phi$, which gives a linear scale.
options.D: The scale is linear because the restoring torque is independent of deflection and current is inversely proportional to deflection.
